title: Singular partitive of -ton/-tön words
summary: For -ton/-tön words, keep the dictionary form and add -ta/-tä: työtön (“unemployed”) → työtöntä.
objectives: Form the singular partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

The ending -ton/-tön often describes being without something. These adjectives keep their dictionary form and add -ta/-tä in singular partitive. Do not form the stronger -ttoma-/-ttömä- stem for this singular case. Vowel harmony follows the complete word.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: Keep työtön and add -tä: työtön → työtöntä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “unemployed”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep onneton and add -ta: onneton → onnetonta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “unhappy”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep koditon and add -ta: koditon → koditonta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “homeless”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep rasvaton and add -ta: rasvaton → rasvatonta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “fat-free”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep sokeriton and add -ta: sokeriton → sokeritonta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “sugar-free”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep maidoton and add -ta: maidoton → maidotonta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “milk-free”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep suolaton and add -ta: suolaton → suolatonta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “salt-free”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep alkoholiton and add -ta: alkoholiton → alkoholitonta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “alcohol-free”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Keep -ton/-tön before the singular case ending.
Do not copy the strong plural stem.
Keep ö and ä in työtöntä.
